## Overview

This project covers **CNC programming** work in **composite and production manufacturing**: translating engineering requirements into **machine-ready programs**, proving toolpaths safely, and supporting **first-article** runs for composite fixtures, trim operations, or metallic/composite hybrid details as assigned.

## Background of the Study

After plies are kitted, many parts require **machined features**—trim edges, holes, pockets, or fixture surfaces—on **CNC mills or routers**. Programming bridges the **engineering drawing** (dimensions, tolerances, datums) and the **physical machine** (spindle, feeds, speeds, fixturing). A documented step-by-step process reduces crashes, scrap, and non-conformance.

## Motivation of the Study

- Produce **repeatable** parts that match drawing tolerances  
- Minimize **machine downtime** with verified programs before production  
- Build a skill stack that complements **kit cutting** and **technical drawing** literacy  
- Apply structured problem-solving from IT/data backgrounds to **CAM and G-code** logic  

## Tools & Equipment

| Item | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| CNC mill / router | Execute programmed toolpaths |
| CAM software | Generate toolpaths from model or drawing |
| Engineering drawing / 3D model | Source of geometry and tolerances |
| Tooling (cutters, drills, compression routers) | Material-specific cutting |
| Dial indicators, edge finders, probes | Establish work coordinate system (WCS) |
| Setup sheet & program list | Operator instructions and revision control |

## Step-by-Step Workflow

### Step 1 — Review engineering data

1. Obtain **latest drawing revision** and any **3D model** (STEP/IGES) if available.  
2. Identify **datums**, **critical dimensions**, and **surface finish** notes.  
3. Confirm **material** (composite sandwich, aluminum fixture, etc.) and **machine** capability.

### Step 2 — Plan machining strategy

1. Decide **operation sequence** (e.g., rough → finish → drill → contour).  
2. Select **tooling** by material and feature size.  
3. Define **fixturing** method (vacuum fixture, hard nest, soft jaws) with lead if needed.

### Step 3 — Build CAM model and stock

1. Import geometry into **CAM**; set stock size with machining allowance.  
2. Define **WCS** aligned to drawing datums.  
3. Add **hold-down clearance** and **tab/stock links** if required for routers.

### Step 4 — Create toolpaths

1. **Facing / roughing** — remove bulk material efficiently.  
2. **Finishing** — achieve contour and tolerance on critical surfaces.  
3. **Drilling / boring** — apply peck cycles where deep holes required.  
4. **Engraving / marking** — part ID if specified on drawing.  
5. Simulate in CAM; check for **collisions, gouges, and uncut material**.

### Step 5 — Post-process and review G-code

1. Post to machine **control format** (e.g., Fanuc-compatible).  
2. Read through **G-code** for obvious errors (wrong units, missing offsets).  
3. Attach **setup sheet**: tools, offsets, speeds/feeds, zero location.

### Step 6 — Machine setup

1. Install tools per setup sheet; measure **length offsets**.  
2. Load fixture; indicate **datum surfaces**; set **G54/G55** work offset.  
3. Load program; run **dry run** or **single-block** at reduced feed if policy requires.

### Step 7 — First-article prove-out

1. Machine **first part** with operator/lead present.  
2. Measure **critical features** (calipers, micrometers, CMM if available).  
3. Document results on **first-article report** (FAI) or traveler.  
4. Adjust offsets or CAM if out of tolerance; re-prove until acceptable.

### Step 8 — Production release

1. Save **approved program revision** to controlled location.  
2. Train operator on any **special notes** (vacuum, dust collection, depth limits).  
3. Mark traveler **CNC complete**; route part to next operation (trim, assembly, QA).

## Quality Control & Safety

- **Never run unproven code** at full speed without simulation and prove-out.  
- **Dust extraction** for composite machining; follow respirator policy.  
- **Emergency stop** awareness; confirm door interlocks functional.  
- **Tool breakage** procedure documented on traveler if FOD risk exists.  

## Sample G-Code Concepts (illustrative)

```{text}
#| eval: false
# Establish plane, units, and safe start
G21          ; metric
G90          ; absolute positioning
G0 Z25       ; retract to safe Z
G0 X0 Y0     ; move to WCS origin
M3 S12000    ; spindle on
G1 Z-2 F200  ; controlled plunge
...          ; contour / finish passes
M5           ; spindle stop
G0 Z25       ; retract
M30          ; program end
```

*Actual feeds, speeds, and offsets come from material supplier charts and shop standards—not generic values.*

- End-to-end **CNC programming** from drawing to first-article  
- **CAM simulation** and G-code review habits  
- **Setup documentation** for repeatable production  
- Integration with **kit cutting** upstream and **drawing interpretation** downstream
